title: Return-By Dates: Extension, Expiry and Cancellation
content:
Every Returns & Exchanges authorization carries a return-by date: the last date on which a first carrier scan counts as on time. These clauses govern extending, expiring and cancelling an authorization.

## Extension

1. > **Retired clause — no longer in force.** The clause providing that a return-by date is extended by the return type's deadline extension days at most the type's extension limit per return has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied.
2. An extension is granted only if it is requested no later than the return-by date of the authorization, with a lead time of 0 days: the return-by date itself still counts.
3. > **Retired clause — no longer in force.** The clause providing that the extension is added in calendar days to the current return-by date has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied.
4. The return must be in status authorized, and the extension is never granted after the return has expired; an expired authorization cannot be reopened and the customer must start a new return, which is possible only if its own window is still open.

## Expiry and cancellation

5. An authorization with no first carrier scan by its return-by date expires on the following day.
6. An authorization is cancelled only while it is in status authorized — once the parcel is scanned it can no longer be cancelled.

## Timing of an extension request

The clock is the authorization's current return-by date as recorded on the return.

| Request date | Extension |
|---|---|
| Before the return-by date | Can be granted |
| On the return-by date | Can be granted (the date itself counts) |
| The day after the return-by date | Not granted |

## By return status

| Return status | Extension | Cancellation |
|---|---|---|
| Authorized | Possible | Possible |
| In transit, received, inspected, settled | Not possible | Not possible — the parcel has been scanned |
| Expired | Not possible; a new return only if its own window is open | Not possible |

Example (hypothetical): a return-by date of 14 June. A request on 14 June can be extended; with no first carrier scan by 14 June and no extension, the authorization expires on 15 June, and from then a new return can be started only if the order's own window is still open.

superseded_clauses: A return-by date is extended by `deadline_extension_days` calendar days at most `deadline_extension_limit` time per return.
